questions.question_english:
75. Evaluate the following statements regarding Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) in India:
A. The Automatic Route does not require prior approval from the Government or RBI for foreign investment.
B. The Government Route necessitates prior approval from the concerned Ministry/Department.
C. Increased FDI inflows assist in bridging the domestic saving-investment gap and facilitate technological spillovers.
D. FDI flows are characterized as volatile short-term speculative capital that can be withdrawn overnight without the creation of physical assets.
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation_english: Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) provides a long-term capital entry through either the automatic or government approval routes, which helps in bridging the domestic investment gap and facilitates technology transfer. Unlike volatile short-term portfolio flows, direct investment involves long-term commitments to physical asset creation and enterprise management. Therefore, the characterization of foreign direct investment as volatile, short-term speculative capital that can be withdrawn overnight is incorrect.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (a) है। प्रत्यक्ष विदेशी निवेश (FDI) स्वचालित या सरकारी अनुमोदन मार्ग के माध्यम से दीर्घकालिक पूंजी प्रवाह प्रदान करता है, जो घरेलू निवेश अंतर को पाटने में मदद करता है और प्रौद्योगिकी के हस्तांतरण को सुविधाजनक बनाता है। अस्थिर अल्पकालिक पोर्टफोलियो प्रवाह के विपरीत, प्रत्यक्ष निवेश भौतिक संपत्ति निर्माण और उद्यम प्रबंधन के लिए दीर्घकालिक प्रतिबद्धताओं को शामिल करता है। इसलिए, विदेशी प्रत्यक्ष निवेश को अस्थिर, अल्पकालिक सट्टा पूंजी के रूप में वर्णित करना जो रातोंरात निकाला जा सकता है, गलत है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) A, B and C only

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Foreign Direct Investment provides longterm capital entry through automatic or government approval routes, helping bridge the domestic investment gap and facilitating technology transfer.

key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Liquidity Trap

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: A liquidity trap is an economic situation where nominal interest rates are extremely low, yet aggregate economic activity remains stagnant and inflation stays subdued.
